title: Unknown last_known_id drops the cutoff and returns every completed digest
reasoning: The route documents last_known_id as the cutoff for polling, but if the supplied UUID is syntactically valid and absent from the database, it silently applies no cutoff. The final query then returns all completed digests rather than reporting an invalid cursor or returning an empty/new-since fallback result. This can happen after retention/deletion of the client's cursor digest and can cause clients to reprocess or redownload the full completed history.
reproduction: Call GET /api/digests/new?last_known_id=<valid UUID not present in digests> when at least one completed digest exists; the response contains all completed digests because no created_at filter is applied.
recommendation: When last_known_id is provided but session.get returns None, return a 404/400 cursor error or define an explicit fallback behavior that does not expand to the full completed history. If fallback to since is desired, allow since to be used only after the missing-id case is handled deliberately.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this route, and the local test search did not find coverage for get_new_digests, /new, or missing last_known_id behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test that creates completed digests, calls /api/digests/new with a valid-but-nonexistent UUID as last_known_id, and asserts the chosen contract, preferably 404 or 400 rather than returning all completed digests.
minimumFixScope: Update get_new_digests to handle a missing last_known_id explicitly and add route-level coverage for that branch.
